description: An introduction to chemistry as the study of matter, its main branches, the work of a chemist, and the importance and everyday applications of chemistry in health, agriculture, industry and the environment.

mcq.questionText: What is the meaning of the word "Chemistry"?

options.text: The study of matter, its composition, properties and changes

mcq.explanation: Chemistry is a physical science concerned with matter, what it is made of, how it behaves and how it changes. Exam Tip: Keywords are matter, composition, properties and change. Option A is biology.

mcq.questionText: The branch of chemistry that deals with compounds of carbon is called:
mcq.explanation: Carbon-containing compounds are studied in organic chemistry. Exam Tip: Organic = carbon compounds (fuels, plastics, food). Inorganic covers the rest.

mcq.questionText: The branch of chemistry that deals with substances that do NOT mainly contain carbon is:
mcq.explanation: Metals, salts and minerals are studied in inorganic chemistry. Exam Tip: Organic and inorganic are opposites. Watch the word "not".

mcq.questionText: The branch of chemistry that deals with the composition of substances and the amounts present is:
mcq.explanation: Finding what a substance contains and how much is analysis, which is analytical chemistry. Exam Tip: Analytical chemistry answers "what is in it?" and "how much?".

mcq.questionText: A person who studies or works in chemistry is called a:
mcq.explanation: The specialist in chemistry is a chemist. Exam Tip: chemistry-chemist, biology-biologist, physics-physicist.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an application of chemistry in agriculture?
mcq.explanation: Chemistry produces fertilizers to enrich soil and pesticides to kill pests. Exam Tip: Chemistry in agriculture = fertilizers, pesticides, soil testing.

mcq.questionText: The branch of chemistry that studies the chemical processes in living organisms is:
mcq.explanation: Bio means life, so the chemistry of life is biochemistry. Exam Tip: Biochemistry covers digestion, respiration and enzymes.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a branch of chemistry?
mcq.explanation: The branches are organic, inorganic, physical, analytical and biochemistry, while astronomy is the study of stars. Exam Tip: Anything outside the five branches is the odd one out.

mcq.questionText: Soaps, detergents and cosmetics are examples of products made through:
mcq.explanation: These manufactured substances are made by chemical processes. Exam Tip: Everyday products such as soap, medicine and plastics are chemistry in daily life.

mcq.questionText: Chemistry contributes to the health sector mainly by:
mcq.explanation: Chemistry is used to manufacture medicines and drugs. Exam Tip: Chemistry in medicine = drug manufacture, disinfectants, testing reagents.

mcq.questionText: The branch of chemistry that deals with energy changes and the rates of reactions is:
mcq.explanation: Energy changes and rates of reactions are studied in physical chemistry. Exam Tip: Physical chemistry links chemistry with physics.

mcq.questionText: Which industry directly depends on chemistry to process crude materials into fuel?
mcq.explanation: Turning crude oil into petrol, diesel and kerosene is a chemical process in the petroleum industry. Exam Tip: Chemistry drives petroleum, cement, fertilizer, paint and plastics industries.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following shows the relationship between chemistry and biology?

options.text: Understanding digestion and respiration in the body
Calculating the area of a farm

mcq.explanation: Digestion and respiration are chemical processes inside organisms. Exam Tip: Chemistry connects to biology (life processes), physics (energy), agriculture and geography.

mcq.questionText: One importance of studying chemistry is to:

options.text: Understand and solve problems related to matter in daily life

mcq.explanation: Chemistry helps us understand and solve real problems in food, water, health and the environment. Exam Tip: Importance = health, agriculture, industry, environment, daily products.

mcq.questionText: Chemistry helps in environmental conservation by:

options.text: Treating water and managing chemical waste safely

mcq.explanation: Chemistry provides water treatment and safe chemical-waste management. Exam Tip: Chemistry protects the environment through water purification, pollution control and waste treatment.

fib.questionText: Chemistry is the study of __________, its composition, properties and changes.
fib.explanation: Matter is the core of the definition of chemistry because chemistry studies its composition, properties and changes. Exam Tip: "Matter" is the core of the definition of chemistry.

fib.questionText: The branch of chemistry that deals with compounds of carbon is __________ chemistry.
fib.explanation: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds. Exam Tip: Organic = carbon; inorganic covers everything else.

fib.questionText: A person who studies chemistry is called a __________.
fib.explanation: The specialist in chemistry is a chemist. Exam Tip: The "-ist" ending names the specialist.

fib.questionText: The branch of chemistry that studies chemical processes in living things is __________.
fib.explanation: Biochemistry deals with the chemistry of living organisms. Exam Tip: Biochemistry covers enzymes, digestion and respiration.

fib.questionText: In agriculture, chemistry is applied to produce __________ that improve soil fertility.
fib.explanation: Fertilizers are made through chemistry to enrich the soil. Exam Tip: Fertilizers supply nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

fib.questionText: The branch of chemistry concerned with the composition of substances and the quantities present is __________ chemistry.
fib.explanation: Analytical chemistry finds what a sample contains and how much. Exam Tip: Analytical chemistry tests what a sample contains and how much.

fib.questionText: Medicines and drugs are products of chemistry applied in the field of __________.
fib.explanation: Chemistry in medicine produces drugs, disinfectants and diagnostic reagents. Exam Tip: Chemistry in medicine covers drugs, disinfectants and diagnostic reagents.

fib.questionText: The branch of chemistry dealing with substances that do not mainly contain carbon is __________ chemistry.
fib.explanation: Inorganic chemistry deals with non-carbon substances such as metals and salts. Exam Tip: Inorganic = non-carbon; organic = carbon compounds.

fib.questionText: Chemistry is applied in the __________ industry to make paints, plastics and soaps.
fib.explanation: Manufacturing industries rely on chemistry to make paints, plastics and soaps. Exam Tip: Manufacturing industries rely on chemistry.

fib.questionText: The physical science that connects with chemistry through energy and forces is __________.
fib.explanation: Physical chemistry applies physics ideas such as energy and forces to chemical reactions. Exam Tip: Physical chemistry applies physics ideas to chemical reactions.

tf.questionText: Chemistry is the study of matter and the changes it undergoes.
tf.explanation: This is the standard definition of chemistry as the study of matter and its changes. Exam Tip: The standard definition of chemistry.

tf.questionText: Organic chemistry deals with the compounds of carbon.
tf.explanation: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds. Exam Tip: Organic = carbon. Keep separate from inorganic.

tf.questionText: Chemistry has no importance in our daily life.
tf.explanation: Chemistry is important in health, agriculture, industry and the environment, so it is very useful in daily life. Exam Tip: "No importance" statements are almost always false in science.

tf.questionText: A person who specialises in chemistry is called a chemist.
tf.explanation: The specialist in chemistry is called a chemist. Exam Tip: Watch reversed pairs like "a chemist studies biology" (false).

tf.questionText: Fertilizers used in farming are products of chemistry.
tf.explanation: Fertilizers are made through chemical processes and connect chemistry with agriculture. Exam Tip: Fertilizers connect chemistry with agriculture.

tf.questionText: Chemistry is completely unrelated to biology.
tf.explanation: Biochemistry links chemistry and biology, so the two are related. Exam Tip: Biochemistry links the two; never "completely unrelated".

tf.questionText: Inorganic chemistry deals mainly with carbon compounds.
tf.explanation: It is organic chemistry that deals with carbon compounds; inorganic deals with non-carbon substances. Exam Tip: The statement swaps organic and inorganic.

tf.questionText: Chemistry contributes to the development of modern society through industry, health and agriculture.
tf.explanation: Chemistry supports modern society through industry, health, agriculture and the environment. Exam Tip: Link "contribution to modern society" to industry, health, agriculture, environment.

tf.questionText: Biochemistry is the study of the chemistry of living organisms.
tf.explanation: Biochemistry studies the chemical processes in living organisms. Exam Tip: Biochemistry = digestion, respiration, enzymes.

tf.questionText: Analytical chemistry is used to find out what a substance is made of and how much is present.
tf.explanation: Analytical chemistry identifies substances and measures their amounts. Exam Tip: Analytical chemistry answers "what?" and "how much?".

summary.correctAnswer: The physical science that studies matter, its composition, properties and the changes it undergoes.
summary.explanation: It is the central science that links to biology, physics and everyday life. Exam Tip: Remember the keywords matter, composition, properties and change.

summary.correctAnswer: Anything that has mass and occupies space.
summary.explanation: Matter is the substance that chemistry studies in all its forms. Exam Tip: If it has mass and takes up space, it is matter.

summary.correctAnswer: The branch of chemistry that deals with compounds of carbon.
summary.explanation: It covers fuels, plastics and food. Exam Tip: Organic = carbon compounds.

summary.correctAnswer: The branch of chemistry that deals with substances that do not mainly contain carbon, such as metals and salts.
summary.explanation: It is the opposite of organic chemistry. Exam Tip: Inorganic = non-carbon substances.

summary.correctAnswer: The branch of chemistry concerned with the composition of substances and the amounts present.
summary.explanation: It answers what a sample contains and how much. Exam Tip: Analytical chemistry answers "what?" and "how much?".

summary.correctAnswer: The branch of chemistry that deals with energy changes and the rates of reactions.
summary.explanation: It links chemistry with physics. Exam Tip: Physical chemistry connects chemistry and physics.

summary.correctAnswer: The branch of chemistry that studies the chemical processes in living organisms.
summary.explanation: It covers digestion, respiration and enzymes. Exam Tip: Biochemistry is the chemistry of life.

summary.correctAnswer: A person who studies or works in chemistry.
summary.explanation: The "-ist" ending names the specialist. Exam Tip: chemistry-chemist, biology-biologist, physics-physicist.

summary.correctAnswer: The ways chemistry helps daily life through health, agriculture, industry and environmental conservation.
summary.explanation: Chemistry helps us understand and solve real problems with matter. Exam Tip: Importance = health, agriculture, industry, environment, daily products.

summary.correctAnswer: Chemical products applied in agriculture to improve soil fertility.
summary.explanation: They supply nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Exam Tip: Fertilizers connect chemistry with agriculture.

hoq.questionText: A laboratory receives a sample of drinking water and is asked to find out which harmful substances it contains and in what amounts. Which branch of chemistry is MOST directly used, and why?

options.text: Organic chemistry, because water contains carbon
Analytical chemistry, because it identifies substances and measures their amounts

hoq.explanation: The task is to identify the substances present and measure their quantities, which is the defining work of analytical chemistry. Exam Tip: Match the TASK to the branch. Water is not alive (rules out D).

hoq.questionText: Match each branch of chemistry with the correct description: (i) Organic (ii) Inorganic (iii) Physical (iv) Biochemistry; P - chemical processes in living things; Q - compounds of carbon; R - energy changes and rates of reactions; S - non-carbon substances such as metals and salts.
hoq.explanation: Organic (i) matches Q carbon compounds, inorganic (ii) matches S non-carbon substances, physical (iii) matches R energy and rates, and biochemistry (iv) matches P living things. Exam Tip: Lock in the surest pairing first (organic = carbon = Q), then eliminate.

hoq.questionText: A new factory in Tanzania will produce fertilizers, treat its waste water before releasing it, and run a laboratory to test product quality. Which combination BEST describes the contribution of chemistry shown here?

options.text: Agriculture (fertilizers), environmental conservation (water treatment) and analytical testing (quality control)

hoq.explanation: Fertilizers show agriculture, treating waste water shows environmental conservation, and testing quality shows analytical chemistry. Exam Tip: Real scenarios show SEVERAL contributions at once. Read each activity separately.
